name: Wild garlic
grown_as: Ramsons, a native woodland bulb grown in damp shade (William's is in the Lower Orchard) for its leaves and flowers in spring. It spreads into carpets.
habit: Each bulb sends up two or three broad leaves 20 to 40 cm and one leafless flower stem of about the same height. Many together make a dense carpet in spring, gone by midsummer.

leaf.arrangement: Two (sometimes one or three) from each bulb, rising from the ground
leaf.outline: Broad elliptic to lance-shaped, 10 to 25 cm by 2 to 7 cm, widest about the middle
leaf.margin: Entire, no teeth, flat or a little wavy
leaf.veins: Fine parallel veins running from base to tip, curving with the outline, with a pale midrib
leaf.surface: Soft, thin, smooth and hairless, bright and slightly glossy; strong garlic smell when crushed
leaf.stalk: 5 to 20 cm, slender, twisted half a turn so the leaf is upside down: the dull paler underside faces up

flower.form: A loose, rounded to flat-topped umbel of open white stars
flower.petals: Six free, narrow, pointed tepals spreading flat into a six-pointed star
flower.centre: Six white stamens with pale yellow anthers and a green three-lobed ovary
flower.behind: Two papery white bracts (the spathe) wrapping the bud, splitting and falling as it opens
flower.carried: 6 to 20 flowers on stalks from one point at the top of a leafless, three-angled stem, facing up
flower.size: Flowers 1.5 to 2 cm across; heads 4 to 6 cm

fruit: Each flower ripens into a green, three-lobed capsule that turns yellowish and splits to show round black seeds; the head stands on a yellowing stem as the leaves collapse.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from bulbs. (From seed: one thin grass-like leaf in the first year.)
winter: Nothing above ground from midsummer until midwinter: the narrow white bulbs rest in the soil. New pointed leaf tips push through in January and February.

leaf: a broad elliptic leaf, pointed, untoothed
fine parallel veins curving from base to tip
bloom: six narrow pointed white tepals spreading flat into a star
a loose umbel of such stars on stalks from one point
a papery spathe falling from below
set: a narrow white bulb, longer than wide, with a few roots
young: pointed leaves pushing up through the soil, rolled at first
crop: two or three broad bright green leaves on stalks from each bulb
flower: white star-flowered umbels on leafless three-angled stems among the broad leaves
seedhead: green three-lobed capsules on the stems, the leaves yellowing and collapsing
dormant: bare soil or leaf litter, nothing above ground

look_alikes: Lily-of-the-valley (poisonous) has leaves in a wrapped pair, no garlic smell and nodding white bells on one side of the stem. Lords-and-ladies (poisonous) has arrow-shaped leaves with netted veins. Autumn crocus (poisonous) has leaves in a tuft with no stalks. Three-cornered leek has narrow keeled leaves and nodding white bells with a green stripe. Always crush and smell.
